intro: Shopify caps the SEO title at 70 characters and the SEO description at 320. Its keyword help recommends 160 characters for the meta description. Google sets no fixed length, and it often writes its own snippet from your page. This guide covers the limits, the Mac steps, and the blank cell trap that can wipe fields during a CSV import.

blocks.text: What Shopify allows in the SEO title and meta description

Every Shopify product has two search fields, the SEO title and the SEO description. Shopify's CSV import help documents up to 70 characters for the SEO title and up to 320 characters for the SEO description. Those are maximums. The Adding keywords help page also recommends 160 characters for a meta description. Use 70 and 160 as your working targets, and treat 320 as a ceiling you should not reach.

rows: No fixed limit, cut to fit device width
blocks.caption: Limits and guidance from Shopify and Google help pages, checked 2026-11-08.

blocks.text: Two details catch people out. First, a blank SEO field does not leave the snippet empty. Shopify's CSV help says a blank SEO title or description falls back to the product Title and Description. Second, a product title that works on its own can run past 70 characters once you add a brand name. Count before you save, not after.

blocks.title: Length is a guide, not a promise
blocks.text: Google publishes no fixed length for snippets. Its title link guidance says titles are truncated as needed, typically to fit the device width. Keep titles at 70 characters or fewer, with the key words first, so less gets cut off.
Why Google often shows text you did not write

This is the part most guides skip. Seer Interactive's SeerSignals data from April 2025 found that 70% of tracked queries showed a Google-written description, not the site's own copy. Individual pages showed 2 to 11 different snippets within one month. Your carefully written description can be replaced by text Google picked from the page.

Google's snippet guidance explains the pattern. Snippets come mainly from page content. Google sometimes uses the meta description when it gives users a more accurate description. There is no fixed length limit. Think of your meta description as a strong hint, not a setting you control.

Seer also ran click-through tests. It compared manual descriptions, GPT-written descriptions and blank descriptions. No version beat another by more than 2 percentage points. Seer's author concludes that routine manual meta-description writing is largely not worth the effort. The exceptions are new pages and compliance-sensitive content. That is one agency's test, so run a small test on your own store before you change how you work.
How to edit the SEO title and meta description on Mac

Open your store admin in Chrome or Safari. Shopify's help pages document the page version of this edit, not the product version. For a page, go to Online Store > Pages, open the page, and click Edit website SEO in the search engine listing preview. The product editor has a similar search listing area, but its exact label and position were not verified. Check the screen in front of you.

items: Open your Shopify admin in Chrome or Safari.
Go to Online Store > Pages, then open the page you want to change.
Click Edit website SEO in the search engine listing preview.
Enter the Page title and Description. Keep the title at 70 characters or fewer.
Click Save, then check the result later in search.

blocks.text: For a product, look for a search engine listing section in the product editor. If the words differ on your screen, press ⌘ F in Chrome and type SEO. Edit the title and description there, then save the product. Each product has its own pair of fields, so the work grows with the catalog.

blocks.title: Read the preview like a shopper
blocks.text: The search engine listing preview shows roughly how your result will look. Read the title first. Check that the product type appears before the brand gets cut off.
Bulk editing with a CSV file, and the blank cell trap

Editing many products one by one is slow. A CSV import is faster. Export your products, change the SEO columns, then import the file with Overwrite products with matching handles selected. Shopify's CSV help says that without that option, rows whose handle matches an existing product are ignored. Choose the option on purpose, not by accident.

blocks.title: One blank column can clear a field
blocks.text: A blank cell in a product CSV import overwrites the existing value with blank when you use overwrite. Shopify documents this in its CSV help. Export a new backup before each import, not only the first one.
Worked example: a product title and description under the limits

Take a wool sock listing. The product name is Merino wool crew socks for men, 3 pack, charcoal. That is 48 characters. Add a placeholder brand suffix, | Example Co, and the title reaches 61 characters. That fits under Shopify's 70 character maximum, with the product words first.

Now the description. Sample copy: Three pairs of charcoal merino crew socks for everyday wear. Cushioned sole, machine washable in cold water. That is 108 characters. It sits under the 160 character recommendation and well under the 320 character maximum. Shorter is not automatically better. Say what the product is and who it suits.

Edge cases matter more than the easy cases. A long product name can push the brand off the end of the title, so drop the brand on those products. Variants can produce near duplicate titles. Google's title guidance says to avoid repeated or boilerplate text, so vary the key words for each product, even when the products look alike.
What bulk editing and paid apps cost you

Time is the first cost. Seer Interactive reports that one e-commerce client spent 22 hours on meta descriptions in Q1 2025. That is one agency case, not a survey. The same article says junior specialists log double-digit hours every month on bulk metadata tickets, with no exact figure. Use those numbers as a prompt to measure your own hours.

Apps add a monthly bill. The Smart SEO AI & Image Optimizer app on the Shopify App Store lists Pro at $14.99 per month, Business at $24.99 per month and Premium at $49.99 per month, billed in USD. Its free plan includes 20 AI generations and an audit of 20 pages. Bulk meta tag optimization appears on the Pro and Business plans. The listing does not say whether bulk covers titles and descriptions separately, so check the app's pricing page before you buy.

Screaming Frog SEO Spider is a desktop crawler with a macOS build for Apple silicon and Intel. Version 25.1 supports macOS. The free version crawls up to 500 URLs. The paid licence is £199 per year. Use it to list titles and descriptions across the store, then sort for blanks and long values.
Common mistakes with product SEO fields

items: Saving the edited file in Numbers' own format instead of CSV.
Writing titles past 70 characters, then expecting the full title to show.
Copying one template title pattern across every product.
Assuming a blank SEO field means the shopper sees nothing.
Importing the whole catalog at once, with no backup and no test file.
Expecting a meta description to change where a page ranks. Google's snippet pages do not claim a ranking effect from meta descriptions.

blocks.text: Where Lazur helps, and where it does not

Lazur is a voice assistant for your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and it answers out loud. Ask where the SEO fields are, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around them. Ask how to edit them, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. It does not click for you, edit your files, or change your Shopify store. You make each change and save it.

Dictation helps with long descriptions. Hold fn, speak the copy, and Lazur types clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Then read it again. Check product names, sizes and materials against your supplier sheet, because a spoken draft can get a word wrong.

Privacy comes first. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Your store data stays in Shopify, so follow your team's rules before you paste customer or supplier details into any tool.
A one-week routine for product SEO fields

Work in batches, so each day has one job. Start with the export and the count. Titles come before descriptions, since the title is the main link text in a result. Then write descriptions for the pages that matter most. Test the import on a few products, then run the full file.
Check the result after you save

Search your store name and a product name in Google. Look at the snippet, then compare it with the title and description you saved. If Google shows different text, that is common. Google sometimes uses other page text, so make sure the page itself has clear product copy too.

Recheck in a few weeks. Google Search Console shows which pages get impressions and clicks, so you can pick the next batch from data, not guesses. Crawl the store with Screaming Frog again and sort for blank or long titles. Repeat the routine until the list is clean.

faq.question: What is the Shopify SEO title character limit?
faq.answer: Shopify's CSV import help lists the SEO title at up to 70 characters. Shopify's keyword help says the page title can be up to 70 characters too. Keep product titles at 70 or fewer, with the product words first, so less gets cut off in results.

faq.question: How long should a Shopify meta description be?
faq.answer: Shopify's keyword help recommends 160 characters for the meta description. The CSV import help allows up to 320 characters for the SEO description. Google sets no fixed length. Aim for 160 or fewer, and say what the product is in the first few words.

faq.question: Why does Google show a different description than the one I wrote?
faq.answer: Google builds snippets mainly from page content. It sometimes uses the meta description when that gives users a more accurate description. In Seer's April 2025 data, 70% of tracked queries showed Google-written text instead of the site's copy.

faq.question: What happens if I leave the SEO description blank?
faq.answer: Shopify's CSV help says a blank SEO title or description falls back to the product Title and Description. Search results may then show product copy. Check a few pages in Google before you assume the field is doing its job.

faq.question: Can I bulk edit SEO titles and descriptions without a CSV file?
faq.answer: The documented route is the CSV import. Third-party sources disagree on whether Shopify's native bulk editor changes SEO fields, so test with one product first. Check the vendor's page before you pay for a bulk feature.

faq.question: Do I need a meta description for every product?
faq.answer: Not always. Google's snippet guidance says to cover critical URLs, such as the home page and popular pages, when you cannot write for every page. Seer says routine manual writing is largely not worth it, except for new and compliance-sensitive pages.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my Shopify product fields for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at things, guides you one click at a time, explains, answers out loud, and drafts or types text. It does not click buttons or edit your files. You make each change and save it in Shopify.

costs.title: Hours on routine copy
costs.text: Seer Interactive reports one e-commerce client spent 22 hours on meta descriptions in Q1 2025. That is one agency case, not a survey. Seer also says junior specialists log double-digit hours every month on bulk metadata tickets. Count your own hours for one month before you decide what the work costs you.

costs.title: Snippets you wrote and never see
costs.text: In Seer's April 2025 data, 70% of tracked queries showed Google-written descriptions. Time spent on exact copy may never reach the shopper on those queries. That is a real cost. It is not a reason to skip the work on new products, where the snippet has less history to lean on.

costs.title: Values wiped by one bad import
costs.text: A blank cell in an overwrite import replaces the existing value with blank. Shopify's CSV help documents this. One bad file can clear descriptions across many products. Fixing that by hand means rewriting each field, which is the same work you tried to save.

costs.title: Subscriptions for bulk tools
costs.text: The Smart SEO AI & Image Optimizer app lists Pro at $14.99 per month, Business at $24.99 per month and Premium at $49.99 per month, billed in USD. Its bulk meta tag features sit on the Pro and Business plans. Check the vendor's pricing page for current terms before you subscribe.

costs.title: Product copy that gets less time
costs.text: Seer moved 22 hours of meta work into product page content. The client then saw a 13% lift in organic traffic to category pages. Seer says this does not establish causation. Treat it as a reason to test your own pages, not as a promise of the same result.

causes.title: Google writes most of the snippet
causes.text: Google builds snippets mainly from page content. It uses the meta description only when it thinks that gives a more accurate description. Seer's April 2025 data found 70% of tracked queries showed Google-written text. Your field is one input, and Google decides what shows.

causes.title: Every product has its own fields
causes.text: Each product carries its own SEO title and description. The work grows with the catalog, not with the number of pages you think about. Variants and copied products create near duplicate text, which is harder to check by hand.

causes.title: Blank fields fall back to product copy
causes.text: When a CSV SEO field is blank, Shopify uses the product Title and Description instead. Teams then assume a meta description exists when the field is actually empty. The result can look fine, but it may not match the copy you planned.

causes.title: Length numbers conflict
causes.text: Shopify documents 70 characters for the SEO title and 320 for the description. Its keyword help recommends 160 for a meta description. Google publishes no fixed limit. Guides online disagree about the right target, so people chase different numbers and never settle on one rule.

causes.title: The bulk route is unclear
causes.text: Sources disagree about whether the admin's bulk editor can change SEO fields. The documented route is the CSV import. Without a clear route, people edit one product at a time, fall behind, and then import in a rush with no backup.

causes.title: Templates repeat across the catalog
causes.text: Google's title guidance says to avoid repeated or boilerplate text. A template that repeats across a catalog runs against that advice. Each product needs words that describe that product, not a pattern copied from the one before it.

fixes.title: Start with the pages that matter
fixes.text: Google's snippet guidance says that if you cannot write descriptions for every page, you should at least cover critical URLs, such as the home page and popular pages. Sort your products by traffic in whatever analytics you use. Start with the top pages, and leave low traffic products on fallback text until you have time.

fixes.title: Back up the CSV before any bulk change
fixes.text: Export your products from the Shopify admin before you edit anything. Save the file with the date in its name, such as products-2026-11-08.csv. If an import goes wrong, you can import the backup with the same overwrite setting to put the old values back.

fixes.title: Edit the CSV in Numbers or Google Sheets
fixes.text: Open the file in Numbers with ⌘ O. Edit only the columns you need. When you finish, choose File > Export To > CSV. Apple's Numbers guide lists Advanced Options for text encoding, so check that setting if accented or special characters look wrong after the import.

fixes.title: Leave out the columns you do not change
fixes.text: A column left out of the file keeps its existing value. Keep the URL handle and Title columns, plus the SEO title and SEO description columns you plan to change. Delete the rest from the file before you import. That keeps the other product data untouched.

fixes.title: Shorten titles by dropping the brand
fixes.text: If a title runs past 70 characters, drop the brand suffix first. Keep the product type and the detail a shopper would type at the front. Google truncates titles to fit the device width, so the words at the front matter most.

fixes.title: Test with a few products first
fixes.text: Import a small test file before you run the full catalog. Open each test product in the admin and read the saved fields. Confirm that blank fields behave the way you expect, then run the full file with the same settings.

fixes.title: Audit the store once with Screaming Frog
fixes.text: Screaming Frog SEO Spider for macOS crawls up to 500 URLs on the free version. Use it to export titles and descriptions, then sort for blanks, duplicates and long values. Larger stores need the paid licence, which the vendor lists at £199 per year for version 25.1.

fixes.title: Put writing time on new and sensitive pages
fixes.text: Seer's author says routine manual meta-description writing is largely not worth the effort. The exceptions are new pages and compliance-sensitive content. Spend your writing time there, and on the product copy shoppers read on the page itself.

plan.label: Day 1
plan.title: Back up and count
plan.text: Export the products CSV from the Shopify admin before you touch anything. Save it with today's date in the file name. Count products with blank SEO fields and titles longer than 70 characters. In Google Sheets, =LEN(A2) gives the character count for cell A2.

plan.label: Day 2
plan.title: Pick the first pages
plan.text: Sort your products by traffic in whatever analytics you use. Mark the top pages you care about most. Copy their current titles and descriptions into a Google Doc, so you can compare them after each change.

plan.label: Day 3
plan.title: Write the titles
plan.text: Write each title at 70 characters or fewer, with the product type first. Drop the brand on long names. Check every count with LEN in Google Sheets before you paste the title into the admin.

plan.label: Day 4
plan.title: Write the descriptions
plan.text: Write descriptions for the marked pages. Aim for 160 characters or fewer. Say what the product is in the first few words. Ask Lazur to draft a few options, then edit the one you like best.

plan.label: Day 5
plan.title: Test the import
plan.text: Remove the SEO columns you are not changing. Keep the URL handle and Title columns. Import a small test file with Overwrite products with matching handles selected. Open each test product in the admin and check the fields.

plan.label: Day 6
plan.title: Full import and a search check
plan.text: Run the full import once the test is clean. Search your store name and a few product names in Google. Post anything odd in a Slack channel so your team can review it.

plan.label: Day 7
plan.title: Audit and sign off
plan.text: Crawl the store with Screaming Frog on the free tier, if your store stays under 500 URLs. Export titles and descriptions. Sort for blanks and long values. Post the list in Slack and agree on the next batch.
